text: Zik stared at the place where the merchant's name had been. The stone had already smoothed over the letters. His breathing had gone shallow. He looked at Ninsun, who was watching his face with a terrible, focused intensity, as though trying to memorize it before it could be taken from her too.

text: The answer was there—he knew, with a certainty that had nothing to do with actually possessing it, that it was there, somewhere behind a wall, behind a door, behind something that had already been carved away and smoothed over before he had even noticed the cutting. He looked down at his palm. The wedge-shaped lines beneath the skin crawled like insects disturbed from beneath a stone.

text: For one terrible, suspended second he could not remember whether Zikir Ashur was his name at all, or simply a name he had been told to answer to.
